text:
katie-sales: FYI Medisync gave a verbal 12-month commit. POC starts Mon. They expect ~600k tokens/day with two profiles: interactive chat during business hours (short replies) and a nightly large-batch summarization job. Asks: recommended reserved GPU sizing, autoscale/burst policy for 30-60m surges, prewarm/KV plan, and short answers for their security checklist (CMK/KMS, VPC egress, 1y audit logs). Need a compact blurb + numbers for the proposal. cc @jason-ssdeng @maria-mlsre @sam-ops

jason-ssdeng: a couple quick clarifiers 1) avg sequence lengths for both flows? 2) p95 latency SLO for chat? those drive GPU counts.

katie-sales: Chat: avg ~48 tokens, p95 <= 350ms (user-facing). Nightly summarization: avg ~1500 tokens, async allowed up to 3s. Peak concurrency estimates: business hrs ~150 concurrent short chats (they said bursts can hit that for 30-60m); nightly batch ~50 concurrent long jobs.

maria-mlsre: Ballpark calc: our tuned runtime on A100-80 yields ~1.6k tokens/s for the selected model variant at target latencies. For the chat peak: assume 150 users * 2 req/s = 300 req/s * 48 tokens = 14.4k tokens/s. 14.4k / 1.6k =~ 9 GPUs. That's raw compute; factor in 20% headroom + maintenance = reserved baseline ~6 GPUs + autoscale to 10 GPUs for burst windows. Nightly summarization is throughput-heavy but low concurrency; route those to burst pool or schedule to avoid overlapping peaks.

sam-ops: Ops suggestion: reserve 6 x A100-80 in the Dedicated pool (gives steady-state + allowance for rolling upgrades). Autoscale policy to add up to +4 burst nodes (spot or cheaper families) for sustained surge windows. Implement a 10-minute rolling KV prewarm before expected peaks. Also recommend a short warmup-run at POC start and a periodic warm job during the 1st week.

jason-ssdeng: I'll draft a compact autoscale + prewarm snippet for the appendix. Paste into the proposal under "Infrastructure plan".

```yaml
autoscale:
  reserved_gpus: 6
  max_total_gpus: 10
  burst_policy:
    scale_out_trigger: qps > 180 for 3m
    cooldown_seconds: 600
    preferred_instance_types: [A100-80, A10G]
prewarm:
  kv_cache: true
  prewarm_window: 10m
  schedule: "cron(50 8-17 * * MON-FRI)"  # run 10m before 09:00-18:00 peaks
```

maria-mlsre: Pricing orientation: recommend two-line quote: (1) reserved capacity fee (monthly) for 6 A100-80 (locked 12mo) and (2) overage/burst billing as per-token + hourly GPU for burst minutes. Rough placeholder for commercial: reserved ~ $36k/mo, estimated burst token consumption ~ 12-18% of monthly tokens -> ~3.0M tokens/month charged at $0.000018/token => ~$54k for burst in heavy months. We'll refine after legal pricing table. Include clause for quantized fallback variant at lower cost if spot capacity unavailable.

katie-sales: Security Qs from their infosec: customer-managed KMS (CMK), VPC peering with strict egress rules, and audit logs retained 12 months. Which deployment mode supports these?

sam-ops: KMS (customer-managed keys), VPC peering, and 12mo audit retention are supported on Dedicated with the private control plane package. Hosted could support some items but requires legal & infra exceptions. Recommendation: sell Dedicated for their commit; note Private (VPC/on-prem) is available if they require air-gap or HSM. I'll attach a short checklist for the appendix: required items + gating for Hosted.

jason-ssdeng: Operational fallback: if reserved pool is degraded, traffic should route to a quantized-compatible replica in another AZ with an explicit degraded SLO (p95 target relaxed to 600-800ms). Add a circuit-breaker that prefers reserved, then burst, then fallback.

katie-sales: Good. Action items: Jason -> autoscale snippet + 2-paragraph fallback description for the appendix. Maria -> concise sizing & pricing line items (reserved fee + burst per-token estimate + fallback discount). Sam -> Dedicated vs Hosted security checklist (one pager). I'll compile and send to Medisync legal tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
